name: Prague
info: Prague is a city on the Vltava river in Bohemia, grown around a castle begun near the end of the 9th century, the seat of the dukes and kings of Bohemia, a residence of emperors and now the capital of the Czech Republic.

facts.founded: Prague Castle was begun by Bořivoj around 880, on a fortified settlement that had existed on the site since 800; legend attributes the city's founding to the duchess Libuše and her husband Přemysl.
facts.where: On the Vltava river in Bohemia, in the Czech Republic, with the castle on the west bank and the fort of Vyšehrad to the south.
facts.known: Prague Castle and St Vitus Cathedral; Charles IV's imperial capital; Charles University; Jan Hus and the Hussite Wars; the court of Rudolf II; the defenestrations of Prague; the Jewish quarter; the Prague Spring and the Velvet Revolution
facts.today: Prague is the capital and largest city of the Czech Republic, with a population of about 1.4 million.

t: Prague grew from a castle of the Přemyslid rulers into the seat of the kings of Bohemia, and under Charles IV, who was crowned emperor in 1355, it became the capital of the Holy Roman Empire.

The city was the centre of the Hussite movement after the burning of Jan Hus in 1415, and the defenestration of 1618 and the defeat at White Mountain in 1620 began its re-Catholicisation and a long decline.
Prague became the capital of Czechoslovakia in 1918, was occupied by Germany in 1939 and by the Warsaw Pact in 1968, and has been the capital of the Czech Republic since 1993.
dyk: The city's four boroughs of Hradčany, Malá Strana, Staré Město and Nové Město were merged into a single entity in 1784 under Joseph II, and the Jewish quarter of Josefov was added in 1850.
ev: Bořivoj builds Prague Castle and moves his seat there
A bishopric is founded in Bohemia, with the bishop's palace on the castle grounds
Charles IV founds the University of Prague and the New Town
The Prague crowd throws the city's councillors from the New Town Hall, and the Hussite Wars follow
The Protestant army is defeated at the Battle of White Mountain
Joseph II merges the four towns of Prague into a single city
German forces enter Prague, and Bohemia and Moravia become a protectorate
The Velvet Revolution ends communist rule in Czechoslovakia

sections.origins:
The land where Prague stands has been settled since the Palaeolithic. Trade routes joining southern and northern Europe passed through it along the Vltava. From around 500 BCE the Celtic Boii were the first inhabitants known by name, and they gave Bohemia its name. They were followed by Germanic tribes, among them the Marcomanni under their king Maroboduus, and the 2nd-century map of Ptolemaios mentioned a Germanic city called Casurgis near the site of Prague. Probably in the 6th century Slavic tribes settled central Bohemia and built fortified settlements, among them Levý Hradec.

Prague Castle began near the end of the 9th century as an enlargement of a fortified settlement that had stood on the site since 800, and its first masonry dates from 885 at the latest. The Přemyslid prince Bořivoj, who with his wife Ludmila was baptised by Methodius, moved his seat from Levý Hradec to Prague and built the castle around 880. The fort of Vyšehrad was founded in the 10th century, some 70 years later than the castle.

Legend attributes the founding of the city to the 8th-century duchess and prophetess Libuše and her husband Přemysl. From her castle at Vyšehrad she is said to have prophesied a great city whose glory would touch the stars, and to have ordered a castle and a town called Praha to be built. The Jewish chronicler David Solomon Ganz claimed that it was founded as Boihaem around 1306 BCE by a king named Boyya. The name Praha has been derived from the Czech práh, 'threshold', from a word for 'ford' or 'rapid', and from the verb pražiti, 'to burn'.
sections.growth:
By the early 10th century the area around and below the castle had become an important trading centre where merchants from all over Europe gathered. In 965 the traveller Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub wrote that Prague had the biggest trade centre. The duchy also drew a significant income from a slave trade in pagan Slavs, sold to al-Andalus in the 10th and 11th centuries. The first stone bridge over the Vltava, the Judith Bridge, was built in 1170. German colonists were invited to Bohemia under Přemysl Otakar I, and the Old Town gained the privilege of a town in 1230, Malá Strana in 1257 and Hradčany in 1320.

The city flourished in the 14th century under Charles IV, who was born in Prague in 1316 and became king in 1346. He founded the university on 7 April 1348 and in the same year founded the New Town, which he laid out himself. He rebuilt the castle and Vyšehrad and built a new bridge over the Vltava in 1357. In 1355 he was crowned emperor, and Prague became the capital of the empire. The city had a mint and was a centre of trade for German and Italian bankers and merchants.

Prague was again a centre of culture under Rudolf II, whose court at the castle drew astronomers such as Tycho Brahe and Johannes Kepler, painters such as Arcimboldo, and alchemists. The city had around 70,000 inhabitants in the 1470s and 80,000 in 1771. Twenty years after the first suburb, Karlín, was created in 1817, the population exceeded 100,000. It reached 676,000 in 1922 after 37 municipalities were incorporated, 850,000 in 1930 and 1,000,000 in 1938.
sections.rulers:
Přemyslid rulers held most of Bohemia from around 900 until 1306, and from Bořivoj onwards the castle was the seat of many Czech rulers. From 1041, and perhaps from 1002, Bohemian dukes and kings were vassals of the Holy Roman Emperors. Vyšehrad was the temporary seat of the rulers under Vratislav II, who took the title of king in 1085, and in 1212 Přemysl Otakar I's royal title became hereditary. Přemysl Otakar II ruled Bohemia, Moravia, Austria, Styria and other lands, and died fighting Rudolf I Habsburg at the Battle of Marchfeld on 26 August 1278. The Přemyslid line ended in 1306 with the assassination of Wenceslaus III.

The Luxembourg dynasty followed with John, crowned on 7 February 1311, then Charles IV and his son Wenceslas IV (1378 to 1419). After the Hussite Wars George of Poděbrady was chosen king in 1458, and the Jagiellonian dynasty ruled until 1526, when the Bohemian estates elected Ferdinand I of the House of Habsburg. Frederick V of the Palatinate was elected king in 1619, but the Habsburg Ferdinand II became king after White Mountain, and the court of the empire later moved to Vienna.

The Holy Roman Empire ended in 1806. Prague was chosen as the capital of Czechoslovakia after the First World War, with Prague Castle as the seat of the president Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk. After 1939 it was the seat of a German protectorate, and after 1945 it was again the capital of Czechoslovakia. In 1993, after the split of Czechoslovakia, it became the capital of the Czech Republic.
sections.life:
Prague was long a city of several peoples. Czech, German and mostly German-speaking Jewish communities lived there, and the city had a German-speaking near-majority in 1848. By 1880 German speakers were 22 per cent of the Old Town and 39 per cent of Josefov, and by 1910 they were about 6 or 7 per cent of the whole city as Czechs arrived from the rest of Bohemia and Moravia. In 1891 the city council ordered that all German inscriptions be removed. German speaking writers such as Franz Kafka, Max Brod and Joseph Roth wrote for a German language newspaper there.

Jews were living in Prague by the end of the 10th century, and the Old New Synagogue of 1270 still stands. The 17th century is considered the Golden Age of Jewish Prague. The community numbered some 15,000 people, about 30 per cent of the population, and was the largest Ashkenazic community in the world. Judah Loew ben Bezalel, the Maharal, served as chief rabbi from 1597 to 1609, and his tomb is in the Old Jewish Cemetery. The gates of the ghetto were opened in 1848, and the former Jewish quarter, renamed Josefov, was incorporated in 1850.

Charles University, founded in 1348, is the oldest university in Central Europe. Under Charles IV everything was built in a grand Gothic style decorated in an art style called the Bohemian school, and rich merchants and nobles added Baroque palaces, churches and gardens in the 18th century. The Czech National Revival from the late 18th century gave Czech literature an important place, and the Czech nationalist party gained a majority on the town council in 1861.
sections.crises:
In 1389 clergy announced that Jews had desecrated the host, and mobs pillaged and burned the Jewish quarter. Nearly the entire Jewish population of the city, about 750 people, was murdered. Jan Hus, a rector at the university, preached in the Bethlehem Chapel from 1402 and was burned at the stake at Constance in 1415. Four years later the people rebelled under the priest Jan Želivský and threw the city's councillors from the New Town Hall, and the Hussite Wars began. Hussite troops under Jan Žižka defeated Sigismund's army at Vítkov in 1420.

On 23 May 1618 Catholic governors were thrown from the windows of Prague Castle, an incident that led to the Thirty Years' War. The Protestants lost at White Mountain on 8 November 1620, and 27 of their leaders were executed in Old Town Square on 21 June 1621. Only Catholicism was permitted and the population fell from 60,000 before the war to 20,000. Saxony attacked the city in 1631, and it suffered a Swedish siege in 1648. A great fire struck in 1689 and plague killed 12,000 to 13,000 people in 1713–14, Maria Theresa expelled the Jews in 1745 and allowed them back in 1748. Prussian bombardment in 1757 destroyed more than a quarter of the city.

German forces entered on 15 March 1939, and most Jews were deported and killed; the Pinkas Synagogue bears the names of 77,297 Czechoslovak Jews killed. Bombing in February 1945 killed more than 700 people. The Prague uprising began on 5 May 1945, and Soviet tanks reached the city on 9 May. About 50,000 Germans fled or were expelled. Warsaw Pact forces invaded on 21 August 1968.
sections.legacy:
Prague is a historical city with Romanesque, Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque architecture. Its archaeological deposits are more than 10 metres deep. Prague Castle is dominated by St Vitus Cathedral, which was begun in 1344 and not completed until the 20th century. The Charles Bridge dates from Charles IV's reign, and the Old New Synagogue of 1270 and the Old Jewish Cemetery recall the Jewish city. The historic centre was inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List in 1992.

The Hussite movement, the defenestrations and the executions of 1621 remain part of the history of the Czech lands. The Prague Spring of 1968, which aimed at a democratic reform of institutions, ended under the invasion, and the protests of 1989, called the Velvet Revolution, freed Czechoslovakia from communist rule. During the communist period little was done to maintain the buildings, and renovation began after its fall. Few Jews remained: the Jewish community numbered about 800 in the early 1990s, against nearly 50,000 before the Second World War.

Prague has been the capital of the Czech Republic since 1993. It is also its largest city, with a population of about 1.4 million and a metropolitan area of about 2.3 million. Its nickname, the City of a Hundred Spires, rests on a count by the 19th-century mathematician Bernard Bolzano.

summary: Prague grew around a castle begun near the end of the 9th century and became the seat of the kings of Bohemia. Charles IV made it an imperial capital in the 14th century, and Hus, the Hussites and White Mountain shaped its later history. It has been the capital of the Czech Republic since 1993.
references: Richard Fidler, The Golden Maze: A Biography of Prague (ABC Books, 2020)
notes: START: the history article says Bořivoj built the castle around 880; the main article says construction began near the end of the 9th century on a settlement dating from 800, with masonry from 885 at the latest. I used c. 880 with circa true.
UNIVERSITY: the history article gives 7 April 1348; the main article gives 1347 in one place and 1348 in the education list. I used 1348.
DEFENESTRATIONS: the history article calls 1419 the first and 1618 the third; the main article calls 1618 the second. I left the numbering out.

CASTLE/CATHEDRAL: the history article says Judith Bridge collapsed in 1342 and the main article says destroyed by flood in 1342 (also 'just before' Charles's reign); I wrote only that Charles built a new bridge in 1357. The main article's 'Hradčany/Malá Strana' account differs from the history article's (New Town of 1257 later renamed Malá Strana); I followed the main article's names, Malá Strana 1257, and gave Hradčany 1320 from the history article.

GERMAN SHARE: 1880 and 1910 shares differ (history: 13.52% and 5.97%; main: 14% and 6.7%); I wrote 'about 6 or 7 per cent' and left the 1880 city-wide figure out. The Old Town and Josefov shares for 1880 are from the history article only.
RUDOLF II: reign dates differ (1576-1612 versus elected 1576 and 1575-1611); I gave no dates for his reign. Hapsburg succession dates were kept to those the articles agree on.
BOMBING 1945: history says over 700 dead, main says 701; I wrote 'more than 700'. The main article also gives a March raid of about 370 dead, left out.
JEWISH POPULATION: 15,000 (about 30%) in the 17th century is from the history article; the main article says about a quarter by 1708. I used the first only.
The main article says Charles Bridge replaced the Judith Bridge; the history article says the 1357 bridge is 'now known as' the Charles Bridge. Fine as written.
The Bohemian kingship: the history article gives 1085 (as Vratislav I) and 1158 for earlier titles and 1212 for the hereditary kingdom, with Přemysl Otakar I; I mentioned 1085 and 1212 only.

Left out: the Swedish capture of the Codex Gigas, economy, tourism, sport, transport, rankings, the 2023 shooting, floods of 2002 and the present city government. The 1,000,000 population in 1938 and 676,000 in 1922 are from the history article's timeline. About 100,000 'around 1837' is derived from 'twenty years' after 1817, as the article states.
The section 'Charles IV laid out the New Town himself' is from the main article; 'inspiration of Paris' left out.
